# Human Endurance Podcast

> Endurance sports podcast hosted by Bruna and Fabi, exploring the science and stories behind human performance in running, triathlon, and ultra-endurance sports.

The Human Endurance Podcast features two series: an Expert Series with specialists in sports science, nutrition, physiology, and coaching, and a Guest Series sharing real stories from everyday athletes balancing full-time lives with extraordinary endurance pursuits like ultras and Ironmans. Hosted by Bruna (runner, coach, NCAA track athlete, co-founder of Augo Training) and Fabi (triathlete, coach, Ironman finisher, co-founder of Augo Training).

## Pages

- [Home](/): Podcast overview, hosts, series, featured episodes, and where to listen.
- [Episodes](/podcast): All 43 episodes with show notes and guests.
- [Blog](/blog): Long-form articles on endurance training, race reports, and interviews.

## Blog posts

- [Your Injury Didn’t Start When It Started Hurting](/blog/martin-kumm-injury-robustness): A WorldTour sports chiropractor on robustness, foot mechanics, and what to stop worrying about
- [Running 100km at 3:47min/km with Pascal Rüeger](/blog/pascal-rueger-100km-swiss-record): Pascal broke the Swiss national record that had stood since 1985 by almost 9 minutes.
- [Marginal Gains for Competitive Age-Groupers](/blog/marginal-gains-for-competitive-age-groupers): New Episode with Mikael Eriksson, founder of Scientific Triathlon & Host of That Triathlon Show
- [Why Cross-Training Might Be the Most Underrated Tool in Endurance Sports](/blog/cross-training-endurance-sports): The 4 Cs of becoming a more complete, resilient, and consistent athlete
- [From Devastating Back Injury at 17 to Going Pro at 32: Nina Derron's Triathlon Journey](/blog/nina-derron-back-injury-to-pro-triathlete): “You can do different things at the same time, but you cannot go a hundred percent at all of them.” - Nina Derron
- [The Journey of Pro Triathlete Leana Bissig: From Uni to T100 Racing](/blog/leana-bissig-uni-to-t100-racing): Patience over quick fixes, progression over pressure, and the truth about transitioning to middle distance
- [Learnings from One of the World's Top Triathlon Coaches, Reto Braendli](/blog/reto-braendli-triathlon-coaching-lessons): Foundation over shortcuts, communication over data, and the truth about training elite triathletes
- [From Medical Student to IRONMAN 70.3 AG World Champion: Samuel Studer](/blog/samuel-studer-ironman-703-world-champion): “I don’t say I don’t have time. I always say it’s just a matter of how you set your priorities” - Samuel
- [Lessons from 31 Ironmans & 25 Years Coaching Triathlon with Coach Joserra](/blog/joserra-31-ironmans-25-years-coaching): Carpe Diem. That was his advice to our listeners.
- [What Elite Athletes Know About Mental Training (That You Don't)](/blog/stu-holliday-mental-training): Turns out mental toughness is as trainable as your VO2 max - if you’re willing to put in the work
- [Key Takeaways from Our Conversation with Coach David Tilbury-Davis](/blog/david-tilbury-davis-triathlon-coaching): Includes: Foundations of triathlon training; Imposter Syndrome; AI in coaching; Lactate; Common mistakes in training
- [The "Soft Approach" to Running Faster with Coach Brian](/blog/coach-brian-soft-approach-running-faster): Our latest episode with Brian Boisvert, a 2h44 marathoner and running coach, offers a fresh perspective on running that goes way beyond finishing times
- [From Marathon to Ultra: What Jazmine Lowther Taught Us About Making the Leap](/blog/jazmine-lowther-marathon-to-ultra): Jasmine Lowther, a Pro Ultra Runner & Coach, 9th @ OCC UTMB 2025, came on the Human Endurance Podcast a few weeks ago to share our knowledge with us. Here's everything we learned.
- [A Practical Guide to Fueling for Performance with Danielle de Francesco](/blog/danielle-de-francesco-fueling-for-performance): What if I told you that the secret to unlocking your athletic potential isn't found in your training plan, but on your dinner plate?
